A micrometer screw gauge is used to measure the diameter of a copper wire.
The reading with the wire in position is shown in diagram 1. The wire is removed and the jaws of
the micrometer are closed. The new reading is shown in diagram 2.

What is the diameter of the wire?

hints: Look at the horizontal sleeve scale in diagram 1 and count how many $0.5\text{ mm}$ divisions are uncovered before the thimble edge, then add the thimble mark near 10.
Recall that each thimble division is $0.01\text{ mm}$ and that diagram 2 with closed jaws should read $0.00\text{ mm}$ if there is no zero error.
Compare the diagram 2 thimble reading near 15 with zero to decide if the zero error is positive and whether the true diameter is observed reading minus zero reading.
walkthrough: Read diagram 1: the sleeve shows $2.5\text{ mm}$ uncovered and the thimble scale reads about $0.10\text{ mm}$, so observed reading $= 2.5 + 0.10 = 2.60\text{ mm}$.
Read diagram 2 with jaws closed: the sleeve shows $0.0\text{ mm}$ but the thimble reads $0.15\text{ mm}$, so zero error $= +0.15\text{ mm}$.
True value corrects for systematic zero error using $\text{true} = \text{observed} - \text{zero error}$.
Substitute with units: $2.60\text{ mm} - 0.15\text{ mm} = 2.45\text{ mm}$.

A.explanation: Subtracting the $0.15\text{ mm}$ zero reading the wrong way or misreading the sleeve gives too small a value.

B.explanation: Observed $2.60\text{ mm}$ minus positive zero error $0.15\text{ mm}$ gives $2.45\text{ mm}$.

C.explanation: This is close to the uncorrected diagram 1 reading of $2.60\text{ mm}$ with no subtraction of the zero error.

D.explanation: Adding the $0.15\text{ mm}$ zero error instead of subtracting it gives $2.75\text{ mm}$, near $2.73\text{ mm}$.
